issues.detail: Both oracle_outputs return (Re/50)^alpha, which is dimensionless and equals one at Re=50. The declared readout lambda_DNS instead means the dimensional/inverse-time Lyapunov exponent extracted from the decorrelator, and its definition never defines a ratio. The source supplies no amplitude with which either AST could return raw lambda_DNS. Rename the common readout to an explicit quantity such as lambda_ratio_to_Re50, define it as the amplitude-free model ratio lambda(Re)/lambda(50) implied by the reported scaling law, set its unit simply to dimensionless, and change both oracle output keys and claim readout_names accordingly. Do not imply that the source tabulates a measured lambda(50); 50 is a source-supported normalization reference for the fitted law.

Both claims currently cite only the same DNS apparatus and perturbation conditions, so the strict review schema has no mutually exclusive private condition with which to define the two worlds. Add a source-anchored intermittent_fluctuations_included condition to the alpha=0.59 claim and a monofractal_kolmogorov_mean_field condition to the alpha=0.5 claim. The first is supported by the paper's conclusion that velocity-gradient fluctuations produce the measured departure; the second by the explicit Ruelle/K41 assumption of one small scale and h=1/3. Keep Re, the normalized readout, the 2pi DNS setup, and the perturbation protocol common, and keep the realized mechanism out of Player-visible text.

The source does not report a second DNS dataset in which the measured largest Lyapunov exponent follows Re^0.5. It presents sqrt(Re) as the Ruelle/Kolmogorov monofractal mean-field prediction and explicitly says it is at odds with the measured exponent; the simultaneously measured mean strain eigenvalue, not lambda_DNS, follows sqrt(Re). The 0.5 claim is therefore acceptable only as the source-explicit counterfactual mechanism world under the same public measurement protocol. Revise its applicability and statement to prevent an author or Oracle from describing it as an observed alternative DNS regime.

The current readout uncertainty describes fit errors on individual raw lambda_DNS values, whereas the AST returns a normalized central power-law curve. The source separately reports alpha=0.59+/-0.04 without naming the plus/minus convention; that uncertainty is correctly marked source_unspecified and should remain claim/parameter provenance. A revised normalized readout should state that its AST is the central relation, that no pointwise uncertainty for the derived ratio is reported, and must not relabel the raw fit error bars as uncertainty on each deterministic Oracle response. The alpha=0.5 theoretical branch has no reported uncertainty.

previous_science_card.assessment: The source supports a matched pair of normalized Lyapunov scaling laws over the DNS Reynolds-number range Re in [50,1400]. The DNS exponent alpha=0.59 is explicitly reported with uncertainty, and the Kolmogorov mean-field prediction lambda ~ sqrt(Re) (alpha=0.5) is explicitly presented as a competing law on the same normalized domain. Both branches are encoded as (Re/50)^alpha using anchored parameters. The source does not report an amplitude for either law, so the normalized form is used without an unreported prefactor. The source supports the DNS range and the two exponents, so case_authoring_ready is true.

previous_science_card.paper_scope: The paper studies the Reynolds-number dependence of the largest Lyapunov exponent in fully developed turbulence using decorrelators, DNS of the Navier-Stokes equation, and the GOY shell model. It reports a universal scaling lambda ~ Re^alpha with alpha=0.59±0.04, departing from the Kolmogorov mean-field prediction lambda ~ sqrt(Re). The selected cluster focuses on the DNS-based normalized Lyapunov scaling over Re in [50,1400].
